body.p: Tools that, once executed, cannot be undone or previewed by AI Positron are considered unsafe. These tools include all tools obtained through the Model Context Protocol integration and tools used to run command lines. By default, for such tools, the end user is explicitly asked in the chat box to allow the tool to run. When prompted, the end user can also choose to always allow a tool to run. In that case, the allowed tool is automatically added to the list of allowed tools on this preferences page.

The text area contains a line-separated list of entries for the tools that are always allowed to run without asking the end user. Each entry starts with a tool name, which must match exactly, unless it contains the * character. The * character acts as a wildcard that matches any sequence of characters.

For the tool that runs command lines (run_command_line), the tool name can be followed by a space and a command key. The command key is a short name that the AI model gives to each command line, made of words separated by underscores, which describes the command line rather than repeating it. For example, the command line p4 opened //demo/spec/... may receive the p4_opened_demo_spec key. When the end user always allows a command line, an entry made of the tool name and the command key, such as run_command_line p4_opened_demo_spec, is added to the list. This way, the end user can always allow a certain command line and still be asked about any other one. The command key of an entry is matched as follows:

ul.li: Without a wildcard, the command key of the entry must be the same as the key of the command line. For example, run_command_line p4_opened allows the p4_opened key, but not the p4_opened_demo_spec key.

With a wildcard, the command key of the entry is a pattern that must match the entire key of the command line. For example, run_command_line p4_opened_* allows every key that starts with p4_opened_, and run_command_line p4_* allows every key that starts with p4_.
Without a command key, the entry allows every command line. This is the case for both run_command_line and run_command_line*.

body.p: The command key is chosen by the AI model to describe the command line; it does not restrict the command line itself. Since the key is chosen by the AI model, the same command line may also receive a slightly different key on another run. Use a wildcard to cover such variations. The Always allow option is not offered for a command line whose key contains the * character.
For MCP tools, each tool call is initially approved individually. For example, when this single tool call is always allowed:

If you want to allow all tool calls to the MCP server, you can manually edit that entry to use the wildcard form brave-search_*.
An entry made only of * characters, or a command key made only of * characters, matches nothing, so it cannot allow every tool or every command line by accident.
This preferences page can be saved at project level if you want to share a certain set of allowed tools with your team members.
